Do not enable for mask/helmet characters unless fully masked/helmeted;
otherwise expressions will look neutral.

Watch the Bilibili tutorial before use. Author space:
https://space.bilibili.com/477349877?spm_id_from=333.1007.0.0
Expression strength; 1 is normal. Lower for anime or animals.

1 vitpose: faster
2 sdpose: less body clipping
3 Scailpose: special body proportions

vivid oversaturated colors, overexposure, static, blurry details, subtitles, style, artwork, painting, frame, still, overall gray, worst quality, low quality, JPEG artifacts, ugly, incomplete, extra fingers, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn face, deformed, disfigured, malformed limbs, fused fingers, still image, cluttered background, three legs, crowded background, walking backwards, ghosting
Full local workflow: see pinned comment on the Bilibili tutorial.

false: disable camera motion
true: enable camera motion

alignment_mode      ON enables RPCA global alignment (enable with multiple people or when the first frame is too small after alignment)

hand_scaling / foot_scaling      independent hand/foot scaling toggles (disable foot scaling if feet look wrong after alignment)

use_shoulder_fk_for_hand      shoulder FK instead of hand FK (enable if hands look wrong after alignment)

offset_stabilizer      temporal offset stabilizer (on by default for full body, off for half body)

offset_stabilizer_x     stabilize along X (default Y only) (off when subject scales are similar, on when very different)

final_offset_alignment      global offset alignment

first_frame_offset_alignment      offset baseline: first frame vs anchor (use first-frame mode for half body or multi-person)

best_hand_search     best hand search across frames

best_neck_search      best neck search across frames (enable if neck looks too long after alignment)

confidence_threshold Slider         unified confidence threshold (default 0.3)

anchor_output_mode      single_frame_multi_person /multi_frame_single_person

output_absolute_coordinates      absolute pixels / normalized 0~1

print_detailed_logs      verbose internal logs
